paper_metadata.title: Unsupervised Quantum Anomaly Detection on Noisy Quantum Processors

experiments.description: Noise-free simulation study of projected quantum-kernel OCSVMs on a subsampled Sparkov credit-card fraud dataset, sweeping anomaly ratio and comparing three hardware-efficient feature maps against a classical RBF-OCSVM baseline.

algorithm.variant: Projected quantum-kernel one-class SVM (qrbf-OCSVM) with hardware-efficient feature maps

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Each 20-dimensional feature vector is encoded into a quantum circuit using hardware-efficient feature maps on 10 qubits; the appendix shows RX and RZ rotations per qubit, with entangling gates depending on the backend-native gate set.
problem_formulation.objective_function: One-class SVM objective: minimize 1/2 ||w||^2 - ρ + (1/(ν l)) Σ_i ξ_i subject to w^T φ(x_i) ≥ ρ - ξ_i and ξ_i ≥ 0; kernelized dual uses K(x_i, x_j).
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Standard OCSVM soft-margin slack variables ξ_i and ν constraint; no additional quantum constraints.

problem_instance.description: Fraud detection on a feature-engineered Sparkov credit-card transaction dataset, subsampled to vary anomaly ratio while keeping 100 anomalous samples fixed and adding normal samples.
problem_instance.dataset_name: Sparkov Credit Card Transactions Fraud Detection Dataset

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic dataset generated by Sparkov for 2019-2020; 1,852,394 total samples, 9,651 fraud transactions (~0.52%). Feature engineering produced 21 variables including label; experiments used a 20-dimensional feature vector after removing the label. Train:test split was 9:1; for r=0.2 the paper reports 450 train and 50 test samples.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Grouped by city/zip to resolve inconsistencies; replaced high-cardinality categorical variables with fraud-rate features; used binary dummies for gender; selected features based on visual inspection and Pearson correlation; subsampled to control anomaly ratio; used 10-fold cross-validation for hyperparameter selection at r=0.01.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Train/test evaluation across anomaly ratios; 10-fold cross-validation for hyperparameter grid search; repeated 10 different dataset splits for r=0.2 to estimate mean and standard deviation; F1 score used as primary metric.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Feature engineering on Sparkov data; tomography snapshots averaged to estimate 1Q-RDMs; projected quantum kernels computed from 1Q-RDMs.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Solve OCSVM dual problem and compute F1 score on train/test splits.

convergence_data.variance_across_runs: 10-fold CV and 10 repeated splits for r=0.2; probabilities of qrbf outperforming rbf estimated from truncated-normal fit.

speedup_claims.caveats: No computational speedup claim is made for the simulation study; the paper reports improved generalization (higher F1) rather than runtime advantage.

experiments.description: Partial state tomography benchmark on IBM Falcon r2 QPU versus simulator, using single-qubit test states to quantify reconstruction error as a function of shot count.

algorithm.variant: Partial state tomography / shadow tomography benchmark

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Prepare single-qubit states |+> and |T> and reconstruct their density matrices from Pauli-basis randomized measurements.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the 1-qubit reduced density matrix ρ from measurement snapshots and compare to the true state.

problem_instance.description: Tomography of two single-qubit states, |+> and |T>, to assess reconstruction precision under finite sampling and hardware drift.

dataset_specification.description: No dataset; benchmark states prepared on hardware and simulator.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Pauli random measurement basis transformations U in {H, HS†, I}; equal shots distributed across X, Y, Z measurement bases.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: For each shot count, the experiment was repeated 100 times; precision measured by Frobenius-norm distance d(ρ, ρ_exp).

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute Frobenius-norm distance between true and reconstructed density matrices.

convergence_data.variance_across_runs: 100 repetitions per shot setting; precision saturates on hardware beyond ~10^3 shots.

speedup_claims.caveats: This is a tomography precision benchmark, not a speedup study. The paper notes that simulator precision continues improving with shots, while hardware precision saturates due to calibration drift.

experiments.description: Hardware benchmark of qrbf-OCSVM anomaly detection on real quantum processors from AQT, IonQ, and IBM, using three hardware-efficient feature maps and comparing train/test F1 against simulator results.

algorithm.variant: Projected quantum-kernel OCSVM on hardware (qrbf-CX, qrbf-ECR, qrbf-RXX)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same 20-dimensional Sparkov feature vectors encoded into 10-qubit hardware-efficient circuits; projected kernels computed from 1Q-RDMs obtained via partial tomography.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Same OCSVM objective as in the simulation experiment, using projected quantum kernels K_γ(x_i, x_j) from 1Q-RDMs.

problem_instance.description: Fraud detection on the feature-engineered Sparkov dataset at anomaly ratio r=0.2.
problem_instance.dataset_name: Sparkov Credit Card Transactions Fraud Detection Dataset

dataset_specification.description: 500-sample subset split into 450 train and 50 test samples; same feature-engineered dataset as in the simulation study.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Same feature engineering and subsampling as the simulation experiment; tomography-based kernel estimation on hardware.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: F1 score on train and test splits; hardware results compared to noise-free simulator; 128 simulator repetitions used to estimate standard deviation in the finite-sampling regime.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Partial tomography on each sample; 1Q-RDM averaging; projected kernel construction.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Train OCSVM and compute F1 on train/test splits.

convergence_data.variance_across_runs: Noise-free simulator repeated 128 times; reported standard deviations of F1: train 0.00209/0.00298/0.00274 and test 0.01457/0.01989/0.01320 for qrbf-CX/ECR/RXX.

speedup_claims.caveats: No runtime speedup is claimed. The paper reports that qrbf models can generalize better than the classical rbf baseline on hardware, but also states that further experimental data analysis is needed to confirm a generalization enhancement in the presence of hardware noise.
